title: Monotonicity of time and success threshold
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, let $T_1,T_2\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and let $p,q\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Q}$. Suppose $T_1(m)\le T_2(m)$ and $q(m)\le p(m)$ for every $m$. If, on every input $x$, $N$ halts on every branch within $T_1(|x|)$ steps and outputs the membership indicator for $L$ with probability at least $p(|x|)$, then it halts within $T_2(|x|)$ steps on every branch and its corresponding output probability is at least $q(|x|)$.
